name: KR Market
intro: Start at the clock tower, then follow the flowers out into the lanes. The morning market spills across the boundary between building and street.

stops.name: The market clock
stops.note: Krishna Rajendra Market opened in 1921. The red façade, clock and repeating arches give this busy trading district a landmark you can pick out above the stalls.
stops.look: Turn the hall until the clock faces you. Follow the alternating light and dark edges down to the shaded arcade.

stops.name: The flower lane
stops.note: Before much of the city wakes up, vendors spread out marigolds, roses and jasmine for buyers who supply florists, temples and weddings.
stops.look: Zoom beneath the awnings. Pick out the orange and yellow flower heaps and the pale garlands beside them.

stops.name: Pete shopfronts
stops.note: Around Avenue Road, rows of narrow shops open onto the pavement. This imagined row brings their shutters, signs, balconies and awnings together on one short frontage.
stops.look: Rotate along the row. The roofline changes from one shop to the next, even where the awnings almost touch.

stops.name: The produce yard
stops.note: The loading yard shows the other side of a market morning. Produce moves from vehicle to crate to stall, sometimes only a few steps at a time.
stops.look: Look down between the stacks to find the handcarts and the paths left open for people carrying loads.

name: Cubbon Park
intro: Cross from the sandstone-coloured domes to the red civic buildings, then take a path into the trees. The smallest stops are a coffee counter and a few books spread across the grass.

stops.name: Vidhana Soudha
stops.note: Vidhana Soudha stands across Dr B. R. Ambedkar Veedhi from the High Court. The broad staircase leads to a colonnade beneath the central dome.
stops.look: Trace the silhouette from the large dome down to the little corner pavilions.

stops.name: Attara Kacheri
stops.note: The High Court’s long red wings face the pale stone of the legislature across the boulevard. A row of columns marks its central entrance.
stops.look: Take a low-angle view to see how the triangular pediments break up the long roof.

stops.name: Filter coffee cart
stops.note: At this imagined breakfast stop, coffee is poured into steel tumblers beside the morning tiffin. The whole kitchen fits beneath a single awning.
stops.look: Look across the counter for the steel filter, the idli steamer and the banana leaves.

stops.name: The bandstand
stops.note: Military bands once played in this open pavilion. Its slender posts let the audience see the musicians from every side.
stops.look: Turn the octagonal roof edge-on and peer between the posts to the paths on the other side.

stops.name: State Central Library
stops.note: The State Central Library occupies the red Seshadri Iyer Memorial Hall. The formal planting beds make a small clearing in front of its entrance.
stops.look: Find the little crest above the central doorway. Its curved edges set it apart from the High Court.

stops.name: The reading lawn
stops.note: Cubbon Reads brought people together to read their own books in silence. This little gathering imagines what that shared quiet looks like from a park path.
stops.look: Zoom into the blankets. Each reader has a book open in a different position.

name: MG Road & Church Street
intro: Watch the Purple Line pass overhead, then drop down to the shop windows. In this miniature, the viaduct, arts boulevard and Church Street fit within a short walk.

stops.name: MG Road Metro
stops.note: A train enters the scene above the street traffic. The station, platforms and viaduct give you a second level of the city to explore.
stops.look: Pause when the train emerges beside the station and rotate to look along its carriages.

stops.name: Rangoli arts boulevard
stops.note: Rangoli Metro Art Center gives the space beside MG Road Metro a life of its own, with galleries and places to stop along the boulevard.
stops.look: Look for the panels along the promenade, then raise the camera to see the rail line above.

stops.name: The pavement bookshop
stops.note: Books are part of Church Street’s identity. This composite shop brings the experience down to pavement level, where browsing can start before you reach the door.
stops.look: Come in close to the frontage. The coloured bands resolve into book spines and stacks.

stops.name: Church Street paving
stops.note: Look down for one of Church Street’s signatures. Patterns in the paving draw on Kasuti embroidery, giving the street a design you can read underfoot.
stops.look: Switch to bird’s-eye and follow the repeating diamonds between the shopfronts.
